but many are deaf to my voice, and hard of heart. Most listen more willingly to the world than to God; they more easily follow the appetite of their flesh than the good pleasure of God. The world promises temporal and small things, and it is served with great greed: I promise the highest and eternal things, and the hearts of mortals grow sluggish. Who serves and obeys me in all things with such great care as the world and its masters are served? <margin>Isaiah 23</margin> "Be ashamed, O Sidon," says the sea. And if you ask the cause, hear why. For a modest stipend, a long journey is run; for eternal life, many hardly lift a foot once from the earth. A cheap price is sought; for a single coin, men sometimes litigate disgracefully; for a vain thing and a small promise, they do not fear to tire themselves day and night.

4. But, oh shame! for the unchanging good, for the priceless reward, for the highest honor and endless glory, they are too lazy to be fatigued even in the slightest. Be ashamed, therefore, you lazy and complaining servant, that they are found more ready for destruction than you are for life. They rejoice more in vanity than you do in truth. Indeed, they are sometimes frustrated in their hope; but my promise deceives no one, nor does it send away empty the one who trusts in me. What I have promised, I will give; what I have said, I will fulfill; provided that one remains faithful in my love until the end. I am the rewarder of all good people, and the strong tester of all the devout.

5. Write my words in your heart, and ponder them diligently; for they will be very necessary in the time of temptation. What you do not understand when you read, you shall know in the day of visitation <note>a period of divine intervention or spiritual trial</note>. I am accustomed to visit my elect in two ways, namely, by temptation and by consolation. And I read two lessons to them daily: one, by rebuking their vices; the other, by exhorting them to the increase of virtues. He who has my words and despises them has that which shall judge him on the last day.

<summary>Christ rebukes the soul for serving worldly interests more diligently than divine ones and explains that spiritual growth requires both trials and comforts.</summary>
<keywords>worldly vanity, eternal life, divine promise, temptation, consolation, spiritual discipline, judgment</keywords>
